_comment: utilities/ subtree lean exclusions. Every entry is a LEAN-ONLY failure (fails under the lean overlay, passes under --base) traced to a DOCUMENTED lean/README.md deviation. Audited: no unfixed bug is parked here. The remaining 28 utilities/ failures fail under BOTH base and lean (base-level concerns, not lean regressions) and are deliberately NOT listed here.
_dev7_frugal_shared_ptr: README deviation 7: the lean shared_ptr/weak_ptr handle is ONE pointer to a { void* elem; uint32_t strong; uint32_t weak; void(*dispose)(cb) } block, with the element pointer stored ONCE in the block. This buys the omissions/traps exercised below: no aliasing ctor, no array support, no allocate_shared, pointer-adjusting (nonzero-offset / MI / virtual-base) conversions trap because there is nowhere to store a per-handle adjusted pointer.
utilities/memory/util.smartptr/util.smar: README deviation 7: std::allocate_shared is an OMITTED entry point in the lean profile ('allocate_shared/allocate_shared_for_overwrite/pmr' are listed as omitted). The test calls std::allocate_shared<int>(ExplicitAllocator<int>(), 0), so it fails to compile ('allocate_shared is not a member of std'). Also touches deviation 1 (custom allocator). make_shared and the shared_ptr(ptr, deleter) ctor remain covered by lean/test/memory.cpp. Lost: allocate_shared explicit-allocator-conversion coverage (inherent to the documented omission).

README deviation 7 (no array support): the lean shared_ptr omits shared_ptr<T[]>, make_shared<T[]> and operator[] (the element count needed to destroy an array does not fit the fixed four-field block). The test constructs std::shared_ptr<int[8]> / std::shared_ptr<int[]> and indexes with operator[], so it fails to compile ('no match for operator[]'). Lost: array shared_ptr subscript coverage (inherent to the documented omission).

README deviation 7 (pointer-adjusting conversions on the one-pointer handle): the test converts a dangling weak_ptr<B> to weak_ptr<A> where 'struct B : virtual A'. A derived-to-virtual-base conversion is a NONZERO-offset conversion whose offset is not statically known and can only be computed by reading the (here already-destroyed) object's vtable. lean's single-pointer handle stores only the block's one shared elem and cannot hold a per-handle adjusted A*; computing/checking the virtual-base adjustment is exactly the pointer-adjusting conversion lean documents as unsupported (traps for MI bases). Base passes only because its two-word handle captured the adjusted A* while the object was still alive. Lost: dangling derived-to-virtual-base weak_ptr conversion coverage (inherent to the one-pointer-handle deviation); single-inheritance (zero-offset) dangling weak_ptr conversions remain covered by lean/test/memory.cpp.
